summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of lethargy, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain in the setting of end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis and type 1 diabetes. Initial concern was for peritonitis, but peritoneal fluid cultures showed no growth, and imaging revealed no acute abnormalities. Symptoms were attributed to worsening gastroparesis and possible viral gastroenteritis, with significant constipation contributing to discomfort. She underwent peritoneal irrigation and was restarted on domperidone with QT monitoring. A right great toe paronychia was managed with nail trimming and topical care after imaging ruled out osteomyelitis. Vaginal symptoms were treated with fluconazole despite negative yeast studies, with consideration for bacterial vaginosis if symptoms persist. Her condition improved with supportive care, and she was discharged home on a bland diet with follow-up plans.
